page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m2.large is a burstable virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. It includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor features a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. Supported instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, AVX-512 Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI), AES cryptography, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it has a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark results place this instance in the lower tiers of performance. In CPU testing, the stress-ng single-core score is 1300.19 and the multi-core score is 2402.69, both falling into the bottom 25% category. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with a read-only large block bandwidth of 20.68 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 16.39 GB/sec. Geekbench metrics show a single-core score of 1045.0 and a multi-core score of 1850.0, which ranks in the bottom 10%. Real-world simulated workloads, such as Redis SET operations at 2.57 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 2.44 GB/sec, also reflect entry-level capabilities.

Given its burstable CPU allocation and low resource density, the ecs.t6-c1m2.large is designed as a budget-friendly option for workloads with low baseline CPU utilization that require occasional bursts. The lack of local storage and low network baseline are key tradeoffs that limit its suitability for data-intensive applications. This instance is best suited for lightweight, non-critical workloads such as low-traffic web serving, basic text processing, development or testing environments, and simple microservices that do not require sustained high-performance compute or memory resources.
